claim: The primary motor cortex coordinates movement preparation and execution through computations in approximately orthogonal subspaces.
source: The primary motor cortex has been shown to coordinate movement preparation and execution through computations in approximately orthogonal subspaces.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known finding from prior research.

claim: The recurrent neural network model recapitulates the temporal evolution of neuronal activity recorded from the primary motor cortex of a macaque monkey during an instructed delayed-reach task.
source: We develop a recurrent neural network model that recapitulates the temporal evolution of neuronal activity recorded from the primary motor cortex of a macaque monkey during an instructed delayed-reach task.
evidence: The authors state they developed a model that reproduces observed neural activity patterns.

claim: The model reproduces the observed dynamic patterns of covariation between neural activity and the direction of motion.
source: In particular, it reproduces the observed dynamic patterns of covariation between neural activity and the direction of motion.
evidence: The authors explicitly state the model reproduces these patterns.

claim: The observed dynamics emerges from a synaptic connectivity structure that depends on the preferred directions of neurons in both preparatory and movement-related epochs.
source: We explore the hypothesis that the observed dynamics emerges from a synaptic connectivity structure that depends on the preferred directions of neurons in both preparatory and movement-related epochs, and we constrain the strength of both synaptic connectivity and external input parameters from data.
evidence: The authors state they explore this hypothesis and constrain parameters from data.

claim: Multiple combinations of feedforward and recurrent connections can reproduce neural activity in the model.
source: While the model can reproduce neural activity for multiple combinations of the feedforward and recurrent connections, the solution that requires minimum external inputs is one where the observed patterns of covariance are shaped by external inputs during movement preparation, while they are dominated by strong direction-specific recurrent connectivity during movement execution.
evidence: The authors explicitly state that multiple parameter combinations can reproduce the data.

claim: The solution requiring minimum external inputs has patterns of covariance shaped by external inputs during movement preparation and dominated by strong direction-specific recurrent connectivity during movement execution.
source: While the model can reproduce neural activity for multiple combinations of the feedforward and recurrent connections, the solution that requires minimum external inputs is one where the observed patterns of covariance are shaped by external inputs during movement preparation, while they are dominated by strong direction-specific recurrent connectivity during movement execution.
evidence: The authors state this is the solution that minimizes external inputs.

claim: The way single-neuron tuning properties change over time can explain the level of orthogonality of preparatory and movement-related subspaces.
source: Our model also demonstrates that the way in which single-neuron tuning properties change over time can explain the level of orthogonality of preparatory and movement-related subspaces.
evidence: The authors explicitly state their model demonstrates this relationship.

claim: The activity of the primary motor cortex during movement preparation and execution plays a key role in the control of voluntary limb movement.
source: The activity of the primary motor cortex (M1) during movement preparation and execution plays a key role in the control of voluntary limb movement (Evarts, 1968; Whishaw et al., 1993; Whishaw, 2000; Graziano et al., 2002; Harrison et al., 2012; Scott, 2012; Brown and Teskey, 2014).
evidence: This is stated with multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Firing rates correlate with task-relevant parameters during the delay period in delayed-reaching tasks, despite no movement occurring.
source: Classic studies of motor preparation were performed in a delayed-reaching task setting, showing that firing rates correlate with task-relevant parameters during the delay period, despite no movement occurring (Hanes and Schall, 1996; Tanji and Evarts, 1976; Churchland et al., 2006a; Churchland et al., 2006b; Messier and Kalaska, 2000; Dorris et al., 1997; Glimcher and Sparks, 1992; Glimcher and Sparks, 1992; Wurtz and Goldberg, 1972; Darlington et al., 2018; Darlington and Lisberger, 2020).
evidence: This is stated with multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Preparatory activity is displayed before non-delayed movements.
source: More recent works have shown that preparatory activity is also displayed before non-delayed movements (Lara et al., 2018), that it is involved in reach correction (Ames et al., 2019), and that when multiple reaches are executed rapidly and continuously, each upcoming reach is prepared by the motor cortical activity while the current reach is in action (Zimnik and Churchland, 2021).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Lara et al., 2018.

claim: Preparatory activity is involved in reach correction.
source: More recent works have shown that preparatory activity is also displayed before non-delayed movements (Lara et al., 2018), that it is involved in reach correction (Ames et al., 2019), and that when multiple reaches are executed rapidly and continuously, each upcoming reach is prepared by the motor cortical activity while the current reach is in action (Zimnik and Churchland, 2021).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Ames et al., 2019.

claim: When multiple reaches are executed rapidly and continuously, each upcoming reach is prepared by motor cortical activity while the current reach is in action.
source: More recent works have shown that preparatory activity is also displayed before non-delayed movements (Lara et al., 2018), that it is involved in reach correction (Ames et al., 2019), and that when multiple reaches are executed rapidly and continuously, each upcoming reach is prepared by the motor cortical activity while the current reach is in action (Zimnik and Churchland, 2021).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Zimnik and Churchland, 2021.

claim: Preparation and execution of different reaches are processed simultaneously without interference in the motor cortex through computation along orthogonal dimensions.
source: Preparation and execution of different reaches are thought to be processed simultaneously without interference in the motor cortex through computation along orthogonal dimensions (Zimnik and Churchland, 2021).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Zimnik and Churchland, 2021.

claim: The preparatory and movement-related subspaces identified by linear dimensionality reduction methods are almost orthogonal.
source: Indeed, the preparatory and movement-related subspaces identified by linear dimensionality reduction methods are almost orthogonal (Elsayed et al., 2016) so that simple linear readouts that transform motor cortical activity into movement commands will not produce premature movement during the planning stage (Kaufman et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Elsayed et al., 2016 and Kaufman et al., 2014.

claim: Simple linear readouts that transform motor cortical activity into movement commands will not produce premature movement during the planning stage due to orthogonal subspaces.
source: Indeed, the preparatory and movement-related subspaces identified by linear dimensionality reduction methods are almost orthogonal (Elsayed et al., 2016) so that simple linear readouts that transform motor cortical activity into movement commands will not produce premature movement during the planning stage (Kaufman et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Kaufman et al., 2014.

claim: A linear transformation can explain the flow of activity from the preparatory subspace to the movement subspace.
source: However, response patterns in these two epochs are nevertheless linked, as demonstrated by the fact that a linear transformation can explain the flow of activity from the preparatory subspace to the movement subspace (Elsayed et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Elsayed et al., 2016.

claim: Inputs from areas upstream to the primary motor cortex have been shown to be necessary to sustain movement generation.
source: A related open question (Malonis et al., 2021) is whether inputs from areas upstream to the primary motor cortex (such as from the thalamus and other cortical regions, here referred to as external inputs) that have been shown to be necessary to sustain movement generation (Sauerbrei et al., 2020) are specific to the type of movement being generated throughout the whole course of the motor action, or if they serve to set the initial conditions for the dynamics of the motor cortical network to evolve as shaped by recurrent connections (Churchland et al., 2012; Shenoy et al., 2013; Hennequin et al., 2014; Sussillo et al., 2015; Kaufman et al., 2016; Vyas et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Sauerbrei et al., 2020.

claim: The dynamics of motor cortical neurons during reaching limb movements has been shown to be low-dimensional.
source: The dynamics of motor cortical neurons during reaching limb movements has been shown to be low-dimensional (Gallego et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Gallego et al., 2018.

claim: Recorded neurons are tuned to the direction of motion both during movement preparation and execution.
source: Recorded neurons are tuned to the direction of motion both during movement preparation and execution, but their preferred direction and amplitude of the tuning function change over time (Hatsopoulos et al., 2007; Churchland and Shenoy, 2007; Rickert et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior work.

claim: Neurons' preferred direction and amplitude of the tuning function change over time.
source: Recorded neurons are tuned to the direction of motion both during movement preparation and execution, but their preferred direction and amplitude of the tuning function change over time (Hatsopoulos et al., 2007; Churchland and Shenoy, 2007; Rickert et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior work.

claim: Major changes in tuning properties happen when the activity flows from the preparatory to the movement-related subspaces.
source: Interestingly, major changes happen when the activity flows from the preparatory to the movement-related subspaces.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: Neuronal selectivity during the task is described by four parameters: two angular variables corresponding to the preferred direction during movement preparation and execution, and two parameters representing the strength of tuning in the two epochs.
source: We describe neuronal selectivity during the task by four parameters: two angular variables corresponding to the preferred direction during movement preparation and execution, respectively; and two parameters that represent the strength of tuning in the two epochs.
evidence: The authors explicitly describe their parameterization approach.

claim: The model's synaptic weights depend on tuning properties of pre and post-synaptic neurons.
source: We characterized the empirical distribution of these parameters, and investigated potential network mechanisms that can generate the observed tuning properties by building a recurrent neural network model, whose synaptic weights depend on tuning properties of pre and post-synaptic neurons, and external inputs can contain information about movement direction.
evidence: The authors explicitly describe the model architecture.

claim: External inputs in the model can contain information about movement direction.
source: We characterized the empirical distribution of these parameters, and investigated potential network mechanisms that can generate the observed tuning properties by building a recurrent neural network model, whose synaptic weights depend on tuning properties of pre and post-synaptic neurons, and external inputs can contain information about movement direction.
evidence: The authors explicitly describe the model architecture.

claim: The model can be transformed into realistic patterns of muscle activity by a linear readout.
source: There are multiple combinations of feedforward and recurrent connections that allow the model to generate neural activity that strongly resembles the one from recordings both at the single-neuron and population level, and that can be transformed into realistic patterns of muscle activity by a linear readout.
evidence: The authors state this as a result of their modeling.

claim: During the delay period, the population activity is shaped by external inputs that are tuned to the preferred directions of the neurons.
source: The resulting solution suggests that different network mechanisms operate during movement preparation and execution. During the delay period, the population activity is shaped by external inputs that are tuned to the preferred directions of the neurons.
evidence: The authors state this as a result from their model inference.

claim: During movement execution, the localized pattern of activity is maintained via strong direction-specific recurrent connections.
source: During movement execution, the localized pattern of activity is maintained via strong direction-specific recurrent connections.
evidence: The authors state this as a result from their model inference.

claim: Multi-electrode recordings were from the primary motor cortex of two macaque monkeys performing an instructed-delay, center-out reaching task.
source: We analyzed multi-electrode recordings from the primary motor cortex (M1) of two macaque monkeys performing a previously reported instructed-delay, center-out reaching task (Rubino et al., 2006).
evidence: The authors describe their data source with a citation.

claim: The task consisted of three periods: a hold period, an instruction period, and a movement period.
source: The task consisted of three periods (Figure 1a): a hold period, during which the monkey was trained to hold the cursor on a center target and wait 500ms for the instruction cue; an instruction period, during which the monkey was presented with one of eight evenly spaced peripheral targets and continued to hold at the center for an additional 1,000–1,500ms; a movement period, signalled by a go cue, when the monkey initiated the reach to the peripheral target.
evidence: The authors describe the task structure and reference Figure 1a.

claim: During the hold period, the monkey held the cursor on a center target and waited 500ms for the instruction cue.
source: a hold period, during which the monkey was trained to hold the cursor on a center target and wait 500ms for the instruction cue
evidence: The authors describe the hold period of the task.

claim: During the instruction period, the monkey was presented with one of eight evenly spaced peripheral targets and continued to hold at the center for an additional 1,000–1,500ms.
source: an instruction period, during which the monkey was presented with one of eight evenly spaced peripheral targets and continued to hold at the center for an additional 1,000–1,500ms
evidence: The authors describe the instruction period of the task.

claim: The movement period was signalled by a go cue, when the monkey initiated the reach to the peripheral target.
source: a movement period, signalled by a go cue, when the monkey initiated the reach to the peripheral target
evidence: The authors describe the movement period of the task.

claim: Successful trials for which the monkeys reached the target were rewarded with a juice or water reward.
source: Successful trials for which the monkeys reached the target were rewarded with a juice or water reward.
evidence: The authors describe the reward structure of the task.

claim: The preparatory and movement-related epochs were defined as two 300ms time intervals beginning, respectively, 100ms after target onset and 50ms before the start of the movement.
source: In line with previous studies (e.g. Elsayed et al., 2016), the preparatory and movement-related epochs were defined as two 300ms time intervals beginning, respectively, 100ms after target onset and 50ms before the start of the movement.
evidence: The authors explicitly define their epoch definitions with a citation.

claim: The population activity profile is spatially localized during both preparatory and execution epochs.
source: Neuronal tuning to movement direction is reflected in a population activity profile that is spatially localized, as shown in Figure 1f-g, were we plot the normalized firing rate for all neurons, as a function of their preferred direction, separately for the two epochs.
evidence: The authors describe the population activity pattern and reference Figure 1f-g.

claim: The activity of single neurons is drastically rearranged across time, while the population activity remains localized around the same angular location.
source: It illustrates how the activity of single neurons is drastically rearranged across time, while the population activity remains localized around the same angular location, which corresponds to the location of the target on the screen.
evidence: The authors describe the relationship between single-neuron and population-level dynamics.

claim: The variability in preferred direction during the delay period alone and during movement execution alone was significantly smaller than the variability during the entire duration of the task.
source: As the variability in preferred direction during the delay period alone and during movement execution alone was significantly smaller than the variability during the entire duration of the task (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), we characterized neurons tuning properties only in terms of these two epochs.
evidence: The authors report a statistical comparison and reference a figure.

claim: There exists two qualitatively distinct regions in the space of parameters characterizing recurrent connectivity: one with weak recurrent connectivity where activity is uniform in the absence of tuned inputs, and one with strong recurrent connectivity where network activity is tuned even without tuned inputs.
source: We found that, similarly to the ring model (Ben-Yishai et al., 1995; Hansel and Sompolinsky, 1998), there exists two qualitatively distinct regions in the space of parameters characterizing recurrent connectivity (Figure 3b). For weak recurrent connectivity (gray area in Figure 3b), the activity in the network is uniform in the absence of tuned inputs. Thus, in this region, tuned network activity must rely on external inputs. For strong recurrent connectivity (white area in Figure 3b), network activity is tuned, even in the absence of tuned inputs.
evidence: The authors describe the phase diagram of their model with citations and reference to a figure.

claim: These two regimes are separated by a bifurcation line, where the uniform solution becomes unstable due to a Turing instability.
source: These two regimes are separated by a bifurcation line, where the uniform solution becomes unstable due to a Turing instability (Ben-Yishai et al., 1995; Hansel and Sompolinsky, 1998).
evidence: The authors describe the bifurcation with citations to prior work.

claim: Recurrent connectivity plays a major role in maintaining the degree of spatial modulation observed in the data.
source: Our analysis therefore suggests that recurrent connectivity plays a major role in maintaining the degree of spatial modulation observed in the data.
evidence: The authors state this as a conclusion from their analysis.

claim: The same analysis applied to a second dataset recorded from a different macaque monkey performing the same task yielded qualitatively similar results.
source: Importantly, the same analysis applied to a second dataset recorded from a different macaque monkey performing the same task yielded qualitatively similar results (see Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The authors report replication of results in a second dataset.

claim: The model generates realistic neural activity at both the single-neuron and population level.
source: We have shown that the model is able to reproduce the dynamics of the order parameters computed from data. Here, we ask how the activity of single neurons in our model compares to data, and whether a readout of neural activity can generate realistic patterns of muscle activity.
evidence: The authors state this as a goal and show results supporting it.

claim: A linear readout of the network activity can generate realistic patterns of muscle activity that closely match electromyographic (EMG) signals recorded from Monkey Bx during a center-out reaching movement.
source: Finally, a linear readout of the activity from simulations can generate realistic patterns of muscle activity, which closely match electromyographic (EMG) signals recorded from Monkey Bx during a center-out reaching movement (Figure 5b).
evidence: The authors report this result with reference to Figure 5b.

claim: Tuning curves from simulations strongly resemble the ones from data.
source: Overall, tuning curves from simulations strongly resemble the ones from data (see Figure 5—figure supplement 3, and Discussion).
evidence: The authors state this comparison with reference to a figure.

claim: Both the activity from recordings and from simulations present sequential activity and rotational dynamics.
source: We also noted that both the activity from recordings and from simulations present sequential activity and rotational dynamics (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The authors report this observation with reference to a figure.

claim: The top principal components of the preparatory activity explain most of the variance of the preparatory activity, but very little variance of the movement-related activity.
source: As previously reported in the literature Kaufman et al., 2014; Elsayed et al., 2016, the top panel in Figure 6a shows that the top principal components of the preparatory activity explain most of the variance of the preparatory activity, but very little variance of the movement-related activity
evidence: The authors report this finding with citations and reference to a figure.

claim: The top movement-related principal components explain very little variance of the preparatory activity.
source: vice versa, the top movement-related principal components explain very little variance of the preparatory activity (Figure 6a, bottom panel).
evidence: The authors report this finding with reference to a figure.

claim: The activity of the network model displays the property that preparatory and movement-related subspaces are approximately orthogonal.
source: The activity of our network model also displays this property (Figure 6b).
evidence: The authors state the model reproduces this property with reference to a figure.

claim: The alignment index is much smaller than the one computed between two subspaces drawn at random, in both data and network simulations.
source: Figure 6c shows that the alignment index is much smaller than the one computed between two subspaces drawn at random (random alignment index, explained in the Methods), in both data and network simulations.
evidence: The authors report this comparison with reference to a figure.

claim: The model provides a scaffold upon which more sophisticated models could be built to explain neural activity underlying more complex tasks.
source: In summary, we proposed a simple model that can explain recordings during a reaching task. It provides a scaffold upon which more sophisticated models could be built, to explain neural activity underlying more complex tasks.
evidence: The authors state this as a conclusion about the utility of their model.

claim: Changes in neural activity that characterize the transition from movement preparation to execution reflect when movement is made but are invariant to movement direction and type.
source: In particular, Kaufman et al., 2016 showed that changes in neural activity that characterize the transition from movement preparation to execution reflect when movement is made but are invariant to movement direction and type, in monkeys performing a reaching task
evidence: The authors cite this finding from Kaufman et al., 2016.

claim: A large, movement non-specific thalamic input to the cortex occurs just before movement onset in mice performing a licking task.
source: Inagaki et al., 2022 detected a large, movement non-specific thalamic input to the cortex just before movement onset, in mice performing a licking task.
evidence: The authors cite this finding from Inagaki et al., 2022.

claim: High-frequency stimulation to interfere with the cerebellar-thalamo-cortical pathway produced reversible motor deficits preceded by substantial changes in motor cortical neuron activity around movement execution, while spatial tuning and early preparatory activity were mostly intact.
source: The authors of Nashef et al., 2019 used high-frequency stimulation to in- terfere with the normal flow of information through the cerebellar-thalamo-cortical (CTC) pathway in monkeys performing a center-out reaching task. This perturbation produced reversible motor deficits, preceded by substantial changes in the activity of motor cortical neurons around movement execution. Interestingly, the spatial tuning of motor cortical cells was unaffected, and their early preparatory activity was mostly intact.
evidence: The authors cite this finding from Nashef et al., 2019.

claim: Cosine tuning functions have been extensively used to describe the firing properties of motor cortical neurons.
source: While cosine tuning functions have been extensively used to describe the firing properties of motor cortical neurons (e.g. Georgopoulos et al., 1982), and they were also hypothesized to be the optimal tuning profile to minimize the expected errors in force production (Todorov, 2002), more recent work has emphasized that tuning functions in the motor cortex present heterogeneous shapes.
evidence: The authors cite this with references to prior work.

claim: Tuning functions in the motor cortex present heterogeneous shapes.
source: While cosine tuning functions have been extensively used to describe the firing properties of motor cortical neurons (e.g. Georgopoulos et al., 1982), and they were also hypothesized to be the optimal tuning profile to minimize the expected errors in force production (Todorov, 2002), more recent work has emphasized that tuning functions in the motor cortex present heterogeneous shapes.
evidence: The authors state this as a finding from recent work.

claim: Tuning functions are well fitted by a sum of a cosine-modulated component and an unstructured component, often including terms with higher spatial frequency.
source: Specifically, the authors of Lalazar et al., 2016 showed that tuning functions are well fitted by a sum of a cosine-modulated component, and an unstructured component, often including terms with higher spatial frequency.
evidence: The authors cite this finding from Lalazar et al., 2016.

claim: The unstructured component of tuning functions is key for a readout of motor cortical activity to reproduce EMG activity.
source: They also argued that the unstructured component is key for a readout of motor cortical activity to reproduce EMG activity.
evidence: The authors cite this argument from Lalazar et al., 2016.

claim: The idea that tuning properties of motor cortical neurons could emerge from direction-specific synaptic connections goes back to the work of Lukashin and Georgopoulos, 1993.
source: The idea that the tuning properties of motor cortical neurons could emerge from direction-specific synaptic connections goes back to the work of Lukashin and Georgopoulos, 1993.
evidence: The authors cite this historical reference.

claim: Localized patterns of activity were formalized as attractor states of the dynamics in networks with strongly specific recurrent connections through the theoretical analysis of the ring model.
source: However, it was with the theoretical analysis of the so called ring model (Amari, 1977; Ben-Yishai et al., 1995; Somers et al., 1995; Hansel and Sompolinsky, 1998) that localized patterns of activity were formalized as attractor states of the dynamics in networks with strongly specific recurrent connections.
evidence: The authors cite this theoretical development with multiple references.

claim: Related models were used to describe maintenance of internal representations of continuous variables in various brain regions.
source: Related models were later used to describe maintenance of internal representations of continuous variables in various brain regions (Zhang, 1996; Redish et al., 1996; McNaughton et al., 1996; Seung et al., 2000; Tsodyks, 1999; Camperi and Wang, 1998; Compte et al., 2000; Samsonovich and McNaughton, 1997; Stringer et al., 2002; Burak and Fiete, 2009)
evidence: The authors cite multiple applications of related models.

claim: Ring models were extended to allow for storage of multiple continuous manifolds to model the firing patterns of place cells in the hippocampus of rodents exploring multiple environments.
source: and were extended to allow for storage of multiple continuous manifolds (Battaglia and Treves, 1998; Romani and Tsodyks, 2010; Monasson and Rosay, 2015) to model the firing patterns of place cells the hippocampus of rodents exploring multiple environments.
evidence: The authors cite extensions of the ring model with references.

claim: The model studied the dynamic interplay between fluctuating external inputs and recurrent currents that causes the activity to flow from the preparatory map to the movement-related one.
source: First, we studied the dynamic interplay between fluctuating external inputs and recurrent currents, that causes the activity to flow from the preparatory map to the movement-related one and, consequently, neurons tuning curves and order parameters to change over time, while at the population level the pattern of activity remains localized around the same location.
evidence: The authors describe a key feature of their model.

claim: An extra dimension representing the degree of participation of single neurons to the population pattern of activity was introduced to decrease the level of orthogonality between preparatory and movement-related subspaces and yield tuning curves resembling data.
source: Then, we introduced an extra dimension representing the degree of participation of single neurons to the population pattern of activity; this is an effective way to introduce neuron-to-neuron variability in the responses, which decreases the level of orthogonality between the preparatory and movement-related subspaces, and yields tuning curves whose shape resembles the one computed from data – in contrast with the classic ring model, where all tuning curves have the same shape.
evidence: The authors describe a key innovation of their model.

claim: In the classic ring model, all tuning curves have the same shape.
source: in contrast with the classic ring model, where all tuning curves have the same shape.
evidence: The authors contrast their model with the classic ring model.

claim: The model is a dynamical system where kinematic parameters can be decoded from the population activity.
source: Our model is thus a dynamical system where kinematic parameters can be decoded from the population activity.
evidence: The authors characterize their model.

claim: The model is constrained to reproduce the dynamics of a few order parameters that are a low-dimensional representation of the activity of recorded neurons.
source: Importantly, our model is constrained to reproduce the dynamics of a few order parameters that are a low-dimensional representation of the activity of recorded neurons.
evidence: The authors describe a key constraint of their model.

claim: The model can recapitulate the heterogeneity of single-unit responses, in contrast to kinematic-encoding models.
source: In contrast to kinematic-encoding models, our model can recapitulate the heterogeneity of single-unit responses.
evidence: The authors contrast their model with kinematic-encoding models.

claim: The advantage of the model with respect to a trained RNN is that it yields a low-rank connectivity matrix which is simple enough to allow for analytical tractability of the dynamics.
source: The advantage of our model with respect to a trained RNN is that it yields a low-rank connectivity matrix which is simple enough to allow for analytical tractability of the dynamics.
evidence: The authors state an advantage of their approach.

claim: The model can be used to test specific hypotheses on the relationship between network connectivity, external inputs and neural dynamics, and on the learning mechanisms that may lead to the emergence of a given connectivity structure.
source: The model can be used to test specific hypotheses on the relationship between network connectivity, external inputs and neural dynamics, and on the learning mechanisms that may lead to the emergence of a given connectivity structure.
evidence: The authors state potential uses of their model.

claim: Neurons' directional tuning properties have been shown to be influenced by many contextual factors.
source: Neurons directional tuning properties have been shown to be influenced by many contextual factors that we neglected in our analysis (Hepp-Reymond et al., 1999; Muir and Lemon, 1983), to depend on the acquisition of new motor skills (Paz et al., 2003; Li et al., 2001; Wise et al., 1998) and other features of movement such as the shoulder abduction/adduction angle even for similar hand kinematic profiles (Scott and Kalaska, 1997; Scott et al., 2001), or the speed of movement for similar trajectories (Churchland and Shenoy, 2007).
evidence: The authors cite multiple factors affecting tuning properties.

claim: The activity in the primary motor cortex covaries with many parameters of movement other than hand kinematics.
source: A large body of work (Scott et al., 2001; Ajemian et al., 2000; Gribble and Scott, 2002; Hepp-Reymond et al., 1999; Todorov, 2000; Holdefer and Miller, 2002; Sergio et al., 2005) has shown that the activity in the primary motor cortex covaries with many parameters of movement other than the hand kinematics – for a review, see Scott, 2003.
evidence: The authors cite a large body of work with a review reference.

claim: The largest signals in motor cortex may not correlate with task-relevant variables at all.
source: More recent studies Michaels et al., 2016; Russo et al., 2018; Sergio et al., 2005; Schroeder et al., 2021 have also suggested that the largest signals in motor cortex may not correlate with task-relevant variables at all.
evidence: The authors cite recent studies suggesting this.
